(born June 13, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall Thundering Herd]] before being selected in the second round by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. After joining the [[Miami Heat]] in 2014, Whiteside was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] in 2016, when he also led the NBA in [[Block (basketball)|blocks]]. He led the league in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] in 2017. He was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and again led the league in blocks in his first season with Portland. Whiteside has also played on [[Chinese Basketball Association|Chinese]], [[Lebanese Basketball League|Lebanese]] and [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican]] teams. ==Early life== Whiteside grew up with six siblings and a single mother.{{cite web|url=http://fiusm.com/2015/02/02/welcoming-whiteside/ |title=Welcoming Whiteside |date=February 2, 2015 |publisher=Fiusm.com |access-date=June 27, 2016}} Born and raised in [[Gastonia, North Carolina]], he attended three high schools in two years within the area: [[Hunter Huss High School]],{{cite web|author=Richard Walker |url=http://www.gastongazette.com/sports/local-sports/gastonia-s-whiteside-back-in-the-nba-1.405563 |title=Gastonia's Whiteside back in the NBA |publisher=Gastongazette.com |date=November 24, 2014 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} [[Ashbrook High School (North Carolina)|Ashbrook High School]], and [[Forestview High School]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} For his junior year of high school in 2006–2007, Whiteside moved in with his father in [[Newark, New Jersey]], playing at [[East Side High School (Newark, New Jersey)|East Side High School]]. After averaging 18 points, 10 rebounds, and 5.5 blocked shots per game, Whiteside went back to North Carolina for the 2007–2008 school year and attended Hope Christian Academy in [[Kings Mountain, North Carolina]]. In 2008–2009, he played prep basketball at [[The Patterson School]] in [[Lenoir, North Carolina]], where he helped lead Patterson to a 34–2 record and a No. 1 national ranking with future Marshall teammate [[DeAndre Kane]]. Whiteside was rated as the No. 19 center in the Class of 2009 according to [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|author=MU Sports Information |url=http://marshall.scout.com/story/812028-herd-men-sign-hassan-whiteside |title=Herd Men Sign Hassan Whiteside |publisher=Marshall.scout.com |date=November 15, 2008 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} and ranked as the No. 87 recruit in the Class of 2009 by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Hassan-Whiteside-83699 |title=Hassan Whiteside |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |access-date=June 27, 2016}} He played in the 2009 [[Reebok]] All-American preview game,{{cite web |author=Hassan Whiteside |url=http://www.herdzone.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hassan_whiteside_477787.html |title=Hassan Whiteside Bio |publisher=Herdzone.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-date=August 25, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825235734/http://www.herdzone.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hassan_whiteside_477787.html |url-status=dead }} and was a member of both the United Celtics (NC) AAU Team and the New Jersey Panthers AAU team as a high schooler.{{cite web|url=http://www.indihoops.com/programs/north-carolina/team-united |title=Team United |publisher=Indihoops.com |access-date=June 27, 2016}} ==College career== Whiteside chose [[Marshall University|Marshall]] over [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte|UNC Charlotte]], [[University of South Carolina|South Carolina]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Auburn University|Auburn]], and [[Mississippi State University|Mississippi State]].{{cite web |author=Hassan Whiteside |url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?recruitId=72045&action=upsell&appRedirect=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player%3frecruitId%3d72045 |title=ESPN Recruiting |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 27, 2016 }}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Whiteside came to [[Marshall University]] under the radar during the start of the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10 season]], but it did not take long for him to make national attention. He was spotlighted in the edition of December 28 of ''[[ESPN The Magazine]]'''s College Basketball column after he amassed 14 points, 17 rebounds and nine blocked shots over 29 minutes in a 60–53 win over the [[2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio University Bobcats]] on November 28.{{cite web |url=http://herdzone.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121809aaa.html |title=Whiteside Featured in Two National Articles |publisher=Herdzone.cstv.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929114913/http://herdzone.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121809aaa.html |archive-date=September 29, 2011 |url-status=dead }} A few weeks later on December 12, Whiteside recorded the Thundering Herd's first [[triple-double]] in a 105–54 rout of the [[Brescia University|Brescia Bearcats]], scoring 17 points, grabbing 14 rebounds and blocking 11 shots.{{cite web|author=Final |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293500276 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606013423/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293500276 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 6, 2011 |title=Marshall vs. Brescia recap |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=December 16, 2009 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} Whiteside would go on to have two more triple-doubles on the year against the [[2009–10 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF Knights]] on January 13, and February 27.{{cite web|author=Final |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300132116 |title=Marshall vs. UCF box score-January 13, 2010 |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=January 13, 2010 |access-date=June 27, 2016}}{{cite web|author=Final/3OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300580276 |title=Marshall vs. UCF box score-February 27, 2010 |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=February 27, 2010 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} He finished the season as the nation's leader in blocked shots with 182, and he also broke the [[Conference USA|C-USA]] record held by [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]]'s [[Jerome Jordan]] for most blocked shots in a single season and the Marshall record for the most blocked shots in a single season and career all in his first year. The 182 blocks were also a national record for a freshman in a single season, topping 177 by [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]]'s [[Shawn Bradley]] in 1990–91. On March 29, 2010, Whiteside declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA draft]], after Marshall head coach, [[Donnie Jones (basketball)|Donnie Jones]], accepted the head coaching job at [[Conference USA]] rival [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF Knights]].{{cite web|url=http://wowktv.com/story.cfm?func=viewstory&storyid=77469 |title=Herd's Whiteside to Turn Pro |publisher=WOWK |access-date=March 29, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726080631/http://wowktv.com/story.cfm?func=viewstory&storyid=77469 |archive-date=July 26, 2011 }} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2010–2012)=== Whiteside was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_select_demarcus_cousins_and_hassan_whiteside_in_2010_nba_draft.html|title=Kings Select DeMarcus Cousins and Hassan Whiteside in 2010 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2010|access-date=December 14, 2018}} He played in the Kings' season opener, recording two fouls in two minutes against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=301027016|title=Kings vs. Timberwolves – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2010|access-date=December 14, 2018}} before failing to appear in another game for the Kings all season.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteha01/gamelog/2011/|title=Hassan Whiteside 2010-11 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 14, 2018}} He spent time with the Kings' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate, the [[Reno Bighorns]], between November 29 and January 9,{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/hassan_whiteside_release_2011_01_09.html|title=Kings Recall Hassan Whiteside|work=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2011|access-date=December 14, 2018}} before being ruled out for four to six months on March 4 after undergoing surgery to repair a partially torn patellar tendon in his left knee.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/press_release_2011_03_04.html|title=Hassan Whiteside Undergoes Successful Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2011|access-date=December 14, 2018}} Between January 1 and February 3 of the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-shortened 2011–12 season, Whiteside was on assignment with the Reno Bighorns.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/press_release_2012_01_02.html|title=Kings Assign Honeycutt and Whiteside to Reno|work=NBA.com|date=January 1, 2012|access-date=December 14, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/whiteside_dleague_release_2012_02_03.html|title=Kings Recall Hassan Whiteside From Reno|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2012|access-date=December 14, 2018}} Between February 15 and April 11, he played in 18 games for the Kings, including having a 10-rebound effort on April 8 against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteha01/gamelog/2012/|title=Hassan Whiteside 2011-12 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 14, 2018}} On July 16, 2012, he was waived by the Kings.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-hassan-whiteside|title=KINGS WAIVE HASSAN WHITESIDE|work=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2012|access-date=October 17, 2013}} joined Chinese NBL team [[Jiangsu Monkey King|Jiangsu Tongxi]], where in 17 games, he averaged 29.6 points, 16.4 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 4.3 blocks per game.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} === and re-joined Iowa.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4897450|title=Kalin Lucas and Hassan Whiteside Rejoin Iowa Energy|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 22, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2016}} ===Miami Heat (2014–2019)=== ====2014–15 season==== On November 24, 2014, Whiteside signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-hassan-whiteside |title=HEAT Signs Hassan Whiteside |work=Nba.com |date=November 24, 2014 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} On December 13, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]],{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-assign-napier-and-whiteside-skyforce |title=HEAT Assign Napier and Whiteside to Skyforce |work=Nba.com |date=December 13, 2014 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} but was recalled two days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-recall-napier-and-whiteside-skyforce |title=HEAT Recall Napier and Whiteside From Skyforce |work=Nba.com |date=December 15, 2014 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} On January 4, 2015, he recorded his first career [[double-double]] with 11 points, 10 rebounds and 5 blocks in an 88–84 win over the recorded a then career-high 23 points, 16 rebounds, 2 steals and 2 blocks in a 104–90 win against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|last=Goodmanjgoodman |first=Joseph |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article6038316.html |title=Hassan Whiteside showing plenty of upside as Miami Heat trumps Los Angeles Clippers |publisher=Miamiherald.com |date=January 11, 2015 |access-date=June 27, 2016}} On January 25, he recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 14 points, 13 rebounds, and franchise record 12 blocks in a 96–84 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Wade, Bosh, Whiteside lead Heat over Bulls 96-84|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150125/MIACHI/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2015|access-date=January Whiteside Makes History with 12 Blocks, Triple-Double|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/hassan-whiteside-miami-heat-triple-double-12-blocks-012615/|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2015|access-date=January the process, Whiteside became just the fourth player in the previous 25 years with at least 12 points, 12 rebounds and 12 blocks in a game, and the first player since [[Manute Bol]] with 12 blocks off the bench in 25 minutes or less. Bol had 13 blocks in 23 minutes.{{cite web|title=Hassan Whiteside does a lot in a little time|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/101857/whiteside-does-a-lot-in-a-little-time|publisher=ESPN|date=January 25, 2015|access-date=February 11, 2015}} On February 4, he scored a then career-high 24 points on 12-of-13 shooting along with 20 rebounds in a loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His 90% field goal shooting and his 20/20 night made him one of only four players in NBA history to achieve such a feat.{{cite web|title=Rubio's return sparks Wolves late in 102-101 win over Heat|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150204/MIAMIN/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2015|access-date=February 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207075223/http://www.nba.com/games/20150204/MIAMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 7, 2015|url-status=dead}} On March 2, 2015, Whiteside got into a fight with [[Alex Len]] of the [[Phoenix Suns]]. The following day, the NBA fined Whiteside $15,000 for his role in the altercation.{{cite web|title = Miami Heat's Hassan Whiteside Tackles Phoenix's Alex Len, Both Players Ejected|url = https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2382942-heats-hassan-whiteside-tackles-phoenixs-alex-len-both-players-ejected|access-date = August 27, 2015|first = Tristan|last = Thornburgh|work=BlearcherReport.com|date=March 2, 2015}} On March 10, he was suspended for one game without pay for striking [[Kelly Olynyk]] during the Heat's March 9 loss to the Boston Celtics.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12455848/hassan-whiteside-miami-heat-suspended-1-game-nba |title=Hassan Whiteside suspended 1 game |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 10, 2015|work=[[NBA.com]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150509043621/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/07/jimmy-butler-kia-2014-15-most-improved-player-award-official-release/|archive-date=May 9, 2015|url-status=dead}} During his first season with the Heat, Whiteside averaged a double-double with 11.8 points and 10 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIA/2015.html|title=2014-15 Miami Heat Roster and Stats|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=2 January 2023}} ====2015–16 season==== On November 1, 2015, Whiteside scored a then career-high 25 points in a 109–89 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151101/HOUMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Heat rally from 21 down, rout Rockets 109-89 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330131140/http://www.nba.com/games/20151101/HOUMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On November 17, he recorded his second career triple-double with 22 points, 14 rebounds and 10 blocks in a loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He became the seventh player in NBA history with multiple points-rebounds-blocks triple-doubles.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151117/MINMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Wiggins scores 24, Wolves hold off Whiteside and Heat 103-91 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330140916/http://www.nba.com/games/20151117/MINMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On November 23, in a game against the New York Knicks, Whiteside blocked five shots, giving him 63 through 13 games. The previous Heat record for blocks at this point of the season belonged to [[Alonzo Mourning]], who had 50 to open the 1998–99 season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/NYKMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Wade, Bosh score 16 each, Heat roll past Knicks 95-78 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610122836/http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/NYKMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On December 9, he recorded three blocks against the Charlotte Hornets, thus opening the season with two or more blocks in all 20 games, trailing only [[Mark Eaton]] (24, 1988–89 with Utah) and [[Shaquille O'Neal]] (23, 1992–93 with Orlando) for longest streaks to start a season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |title=Hornets beat Heat 99-81 for third straight victory |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151209202756/http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 9, 2015 |url-status=dead }} His streak ended at 21 after he failed to record a block on December 13 against the Memphis Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteha01/gamelog/2016/ |title=Hassan Whiteside 2015-16 Game Log |publisher=Basketball-reference.com |access-date=June 27, 2016}} On January 15, 2016, Whiteside recorded his third career triple-double with 19 points, 17 rebounds and 11 blocked shots in a 98–95 win over the Denver Nuggets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160115/MIADEN/gameinfo.html |title=Whiteside's triple-double rallies Heat past Nuggets, 98-95 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331024628/http://www.nba.com/games/20160115/MIADEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 31, 2016 |url-status=dead }} Between January 22 and February 2, he missed six games with a left hip injury. He returned to action on February 3, recording 10 points, nine rebounds and five blocks in 17 minutes off the bench in a 93–90 win over the Dallas Mavericks.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160203/MIADAL/gameinfo.html |title=Wade's bounce-back, Bosh's 20 lead Heat over Mavericks 93-90 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610131007/http://www.nba.com/games/20160203/MIADAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |url-status=dead }} Two days later, he recorded his third triple-double of the season and fourth of his career with 10 points, 10 rebounds and 10 blocked shots in 27 minutes off the bench in a 98–95 win over the Charlotte Hornets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |title=Whiteside gets triple-double as Heat hold off Hornets |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331073325/http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 31, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On February 20, he recorded 25 points and 23 rebounds off the bench in a 114–94 win over the Washington Wizards, marking just the 11th time in NBA history that a player has had at least 20 points and 20 rebounds in a game off the bench. Whiteside also blocked two shots in that game, giving him 300 with the Heat in 94 games, which is the fastest a Heat player has reached the 300-block mark. [[Alonzo Mourning]] was the previous fastest as he needed 108 games to accomplish the feat.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/WASMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Whiteside has 25 points, 23 rebounds; Heat beat Wizards |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209230443/http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/WASMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 9, 2017 |url-status=dead }} In the Heat's next game the following day against the Indiana Pacers, Whiteside grabbed his 1,000th career rebound in his 95th game, marking the fastest anyone has reached that milestone in Heat history, ahead of Alonzo Mourning (96), [[Kevin Willis]] (98) and [[Shaquille O'Neal]] (99).{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160222/INDMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Dragic scores 24, Heat rally and beat Pacers 101-93 in OT |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160620035736/http://www.nba.com/games/20160222/INDMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 20, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On March 1, he recorded a career-high 26 points and 14 rebounds in a 129–111 win over the Chicago Bulls.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160301/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Heat set franchise shooting record, roll past Bulls 129-111 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303112741/http://www.nba.com/games/20160301/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead }} He topped that mark on March 28, scoring 27 points in a 110–99 win over the Brooklyn Nets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160328/BKNMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Wade gets 30, Heat pull away from Nets 110-99 |work=Nba.com |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613084930/http://www.nba.com/games/20160328/BKNMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 13, 2016 |url-status=dead }} The Heat finished the regular season as the third seed in the Eastern Conference with a 48–34 record. Whiteside finished as the league's leading shot-blocker in 2015–16, and he earned selection to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]]. In the first round of the playoffs, the Heat faced the sixth-seeded [[Charlotte Hornets]], and in a Game 1 win on April 17, Whiteside made his postseason debut with 21 points and 11 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|title=Deng scores 31 points, Heat rout Hornets 123-91 in Game 1|work=NBA.com|date=April 17, 2016|access-date=April 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417230131/http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 17, 2016|url-status=dead}} The Heat went on to lose to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the second round.{{Cite web|date=16 May 2016|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400875896|title=Kyle Lowry's 35 help Raptors win another Game 7, reach East finals|work=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|access-date=2 January 2023|location=Cleveland}} ====2016–17 season==== On July 7, 2016, Whiteside re-signed with the Heat on a four-year, $98 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-hassan-whiteside|title=HEAT Re-Signs Hassan Whiteside|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Doyle|first=Ricky|url=http://nesn.com/2016/07/hassan-whiteside-returning-to-heat-on-reported-four-year-max-contract/|title=Hassan Whiteside Returning To Heat On Reported Four-Year Max Contract|work=NESN.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}} Whiteside became the first player in NBA history to go from a league minimum salary to a max level contract.{{cite web|title=Report: Kings signing Hassan Whiteside|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/11/25/report-kings-signing-hassan-whiteside/|date=November 25, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 8, 2020}} In the Heat's season opener on October 26, Whiteside recorded 18 points, 14 rebounds and four blocked shots in a 108–96 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899378|title=Whiteside powers Heat to season-opening win|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} On October 30, he tied his career high with 27 points and grabbed 15 rebounds in a 106–99 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899487|title=Leonard comes up big late, Spurs top Heat 106-99|work=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}} With 21 points and 16 rebounds against the [[Toronto Raptors]] on November 4, Whiteside recorded his fifth straight double-double, a franchise record streak to open a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899521|title=DeRozan's 34 points push Raptors past Heat 96-87|work=ESPN.com|date=November 4, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016}} On November 10, he recorded 20 points and 20 rebounds against the [[Chicago Bulls]] for his third career 20–20 game. The only player to have more in a Heat uniform is [[Rony Seikaly]], with 12.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899568|title=Wade a winner again in Miami, Bulls top Heat 98-95|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2016|access-date=November 10, 2016}} Five days later, he scored 19 points and grabbed an NBA season-high 25 rebounds in a 93–90 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899604|title=Hawks win again, hang on top reeling Heat 93-90|work=ESPN.com|date=November 15, 2016|access-date=November 15, 2016}} On November 21, in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Whiteside set a career high with 32 points while reaching double digits in rebounds for the 13th consecutive game to start the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899649|title=Embiid leads 76ers over Heat 101-94 for 4th straight at home|work=ESPN.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 22, 2016}} On December 14, he recorded 26 points and 22 rebounds in a 95–89 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]], marking his fourth career 20–20 game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899819|title=Whiteside gets 26 points, 22 boards as Heat top Pacers 95-89|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}} Whiteside went on to miss four games in early January with a right retinal contusion.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899982|title=Redick and Paul help Clippers overpower Heat 98-86|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2017|access-date=January 8, 2017}} On February 1, 2017, Whiteside grabbed his 2,000th rebound in a 116–93 win over Atlanta; he finished the game with 18 points and 18 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899397|title=No contest: Heat push streak to 9, roll Hawks 116-93|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}} Three days later, he scored 30 points and grabbed 20 rebounds in just 27 minutes in a 125–102 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], extending Miami's winning streak to 10. The 30–20 game was the first of his career, and the ninth in Heat history including playoffs.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900163|title=Hassan Whiteside explodes with 30 points, 20 rebounds in 3 quarters; Heat roll over 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=February 4, 2017|access-date=February 4, 2017}} He joined [[Bill Laimbeer]] as the only players in NBA history to post a 30-point, 20-rebound game in no more than 27 minutes—Laimbeer did it in the 1984–85 season.{{cite web|last=Winfield|first=Kristian|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/2/4/14512458/hassan-whiteside-nba-history-points-rebounds-heat-vs-76ers|title=Hassan Whiteside put up a ridiculous 30 points and 20 rebounds in 27 minutes|work=SBNation.com|date=February 4, 2017|access-date=February 7, 2017}} On March 12, he had 26 points and 21 rebounds in a 102–98 loss to Indiana. It was Whiteside's fifth 20/20 game this season. He also tied his career high with 10 offensive rebounds in the game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900382|title=George leads Pacers with 28 points in 102-98 win over Heat|work=ESPN.com|date=March 12, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017}} On March 21, he had a 23-point, 14-rebound performance in a 112–97 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He reached 936 rebounds for the season during the game, setting a single-season franchise record by going two above Seikaly's 1991–92 total (934). Whiteside also recorded his 57th double-digit rebound game of the season, a Heat record—one more than Seikaly in 1991–92.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900448|title=Hassan Whiteside sets Heat single-season rebound record, then exits with cut|work=ESPN.com|date=March 21, 2017|access-date=March 22, 2017}} On April 2 against Denver, Whiteside became the first Heat player to record 1,000 points and 1,000 rebounds in a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899444|title=Gallinari carries desperate Nuggets past Heat, 116-113|work=ESPN.com|date=April 2, 2017|access-date=April 2, 2017}} Whiteside finished the season as the league's leading rebounder.{{Cite web|access-date=2 January 2023|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player/_/season/2017/seasontype/2/table/general/sort/avgRebounds/dir/desc|title=NBA Player Stats 2016-17|work=ESPN}} ====2017–18 season==== In the Heat's season opener against the [[Orlando Magic]] on October 18, 2017, Whiteside had 26 points and 22 rebounds in a 116–109 loss,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974702|title=Fournier, Magic hold off Heat 116-109 in opener|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}} becoming the first player since [[Kevin Garnett]] in 2007 to score at least 20 points and grab at least 20 rebounds on opening night.{{cite web|last=Navarro|first=Manny|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/heat-check/article179652136.html|title=Whiteside didn't enjoy his eighth career 20/20 performance because the Heat lost again|work=MiamiHerald.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 19, 2017}} On November 1, 2017, he returned from a five-game absence with a bruised knee and scored 13 points and grabbed 14 rebounds in a 97–91 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974861|title=Happy birthday: Heat top Bulls 97-91 to end 3-game slide|work=ESPN.com|date=November 1, 2017|access-date=November 2, 2017}} On December 26, 2017, he returned from an 11-game absence with a bone bruise in his left knee and had seven points and eight rebounds in 18 minutes in a 107–89 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975246|title=Heat rally in 4th, top struggling Magic 107-89|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2017}} On January 17, 2018, he had a season-high 27 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks to lead the Heat to a 106–101 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975405|title=Whiteside leads Heat to 106-101 win over Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2018|access-date=January 17, 2018}} Whiteside missed nine games in March with a hip injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975871|title=Heat close in on clinching, top Bulls 103-92|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2018|access-date=March 30, 2018}} ====2018–19 season==== On October 29, 2018, Whiteside had an NBA season-high 24 rebounds to go with 16 points and five blocked shots in a 123–113 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070770|title=Kings run away after halftime, top Heat 123-113|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=October 29, 2018}} On November 7, he had 29 points, 20 rebounds and an NBA season-high nine blocked shots in a 95–88 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Whiteside had eight blocked shots in the first half, setting a Heat record for any half; the previous first-half mark was seven by [[Alonzo Mourning]] in 1999, while the second-half mark is seven by Whiteside.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070837|title=Whiteside dominates, Heat top Spurs 95-88|work=ESPN.com|date=November 7, 2018|access-date=November 7, 2018}} On November 20, he had 21 points and 23 rebounds in a 104–92 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070931|title=Russell, Nets add to Miami's home misery, top Heat 104-92|work=ESPN.com|date=November 20, 2018|access-date=November 20, 2018}} In March 2019, he was relegated to a reserve role after coming off a hip injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071638|title=Kelly Olynyk, Hassan Whiteside lead Heat over Hornets 91-84|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2019}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2020)=== On July 6, 2019, Whiteside was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as part of a four-team trade also involving the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/7/6/blazers-acquire-hassan-whiteside|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE HASSAN WHITESIDE FROM MIAMI IN MULTI-TEAM DEAL|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019}} On November 29, 2019, Whiteside scored 8 points, grabbed 15 rebounds and recorded a season-high 10 blocks. His 10 blocks set a Trail Blazers' franchise record for blocks in a single game. The previous record holder was [[Bill Walton]] who recorded 9 blocks in two different occasions.{{cite web|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2019/11/30/20989021/trail-blazers-records-single-game-blocks-hassan-whiteside-bulls-video|title=Hassan Whiteside Sets Blazers Single-Game Record with 10 Blocks|publisher=Blazer's Edge|date=November 30, 2019|access-date=June 23, 2020}} ===Return to Sacramento (2020–2021)=== On November 27, 2020, the [[Sacramento Kings]] announced that they had signed Whiteside to a one-year contract.{{cite web |title=Kings Sign Hassan Whiteside |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-hassan-whiteside |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 21, 2021 |date=November 27, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Report: Kings signing Hassan Whiteside|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/11/25/report-kings-signing-hassan-whiteside/|date=November 25, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 8, 2020}} ===Utah Jazz (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Whiteside signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-rudy-gay-and-hassan-whiteside|title=Utah Jazz sign Rudy Gay and Hassan Whiteside|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}} He spent the season as backup to [[Rudy Gobert]]. Despite playing only 17.9 minutes per game, Whiteside averaged 1.6 blocks per game, ranking 8th in the league in that category.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/UTA/2022.html|title=2021-22 Utah Jazz Roster and Stats|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=2 January 2023}} ===Piratas de Quebradillas (2023)=== On March 14, 2023, Whiteside signed with the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web|title=Hassan Whiteside, Brandon Knight sign with Puerto Rican team|url=https://hoopshype.com/2023/03/14/hassan-whiteside-brandon-knight-sign-with-puerto-rican-team/|website=HoopsHype.com|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 14, 2023}} On February 13, 2024, Whiteside informed the Piratas de Quebradillas management of his retirement from basketball.{{cite web|title=Hassan Whiteside retires from basketball|url=https://basketnews.com/news-201856-hassan-whiteside-retires-from-basketball.html|website=BasketNews.com|date=February 13, 2024|access-date=February 16, 2024}} ===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2025)=== On April 7, 2025, Whiteside signed officially with the [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web |title=Bomba en el BSN! Los Cangrejeros de Santurce anuncian la firma del refuerzo Hassan Whiteside |url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/los-cangrejeros-anuncian-la-firma-de-hassan-whiteside/ |website=primerahora.com |publisher=Primera Hora |access-date=9 April 2025}} He also confirmed he didn't retire, he took a one year hiatus to recover from a shoulder injury which required him to have surgery.{{cite web |last1=Figueroa Loza |first1=Jorge |title=“Nunca dije que me retiré”: Hassan Whiteside de vuelta al BSN con los Cangrejeros 2010|first=Chuck|last= Mcgill|access-date=February 9, 2015}} His father played in the [[National Football League|NFL]] for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] from 1983 to 1984. Whiteside has a younger brother named Nassan, who has [[autism]].{{citation needed|date=December 2025}} In 2012, Nassan's Place was incorporated in the state of New Jersey as a non-profit organization.[http://www.njtvonline.org/news/uncategorized/5k-to-raise-money-to-open-an-educational-center-for-autistic-children/ 5K to Raise Money to Open Educational Center for Autistic Children] Nassan's Place provides low to moderate income families the opportunity to receive quality and affordable care for their children in a safe and carefree environment.[http://hauteliving.com/2016/04/hassan-whiteside-to-host-nassans-place-fundraiser-at-komodo/606872/ Hassan Whiteside to Host Nassan’s Place Fundraiser at Komodo] In January 2017, Whiteside wired $2.75 million to attorney [[Michael Avenatti]] as the first payment in a $3 million-settlement with ex-girlfriend Alexis Gardner, who was represented by Avenatti in the settlement. Avenatti allegedly embezzled all but $194,000 of the $3 million that Whiteside paid in total, even though he was legally entitled to only a little more than $1 million in legal fees. This news came to light during an April 10, 2019 indictment of Avenatti by a federal grand jury in [[Santa Ana, California]]. "We entered into a mutually agreed upon settlement more than two years ago following the end of our relationship; a settlement that reflected Alexis' investment of time and support over a number of years as Hassan pursued a career in the NBA," Whiteside and Gardner told ''[[The Los Angeles Times]]'' in a statement released by his agent.{{cite
